name: skye-advanced-pattern-pack
purpose: Production-minded implementation patterns that actually use Motion, GSAP, Lenis, Three.js, React Three Fiber, Drei, and postprocessing.
rule: Agents must pull open-source recipes first, then one of these implementation patterns before building a premium public surface. Do not merely describe motion or 3D; use a pattern, wire real imports into source, and pass design_stack_audit.
auditRule: Package installs, prose, static canvas substitutes, and repeated dark card templates fail. Required open-source stack must be imported and visibly used in runtime source.

patterns.title: Cinematic Command Hero
patterns.quality: Full-width editorial headline, living WebGL command object, proof strip, CTA, reduced-motion-safe composition.

patterns.title: Scroll Proof Funnel
patterns.quality: Pinned/scrubbed funnel for process storytelling without turning the page into cards and paragraphs.

patterns.title: Neon Motion Chrome
patterns.quality: Legal Skyes-style neon scrollbar plus scroll progress, scanline atmosphere, pointer-reactive cursor glow, shimmer text utilities, magnetic hover utilities, mobile and reduced-motion fallbacks.

patterns.title: SkyeSol Living Background
patterns.quality: SkyeSol-style alive backdrop: fixed transparent canvas, aurora wave bands, gold/violet/cyan particles, pointer parallax, grain, scanline, capped DPR, mobile particle reduction, and reduced-motion fallback.

patterns.title: App-First Command Center
patterns.quality: The first viewport is the tool surface itself: tabs, status, controls, proof, and action density.

patterns.title: Editorial Proof Atlas
patterns.quality: Magazine-like proof story with one dominant media surface, sparse evidence, and warm editorial palette. Built to avoid dark dashboard repetition.

patterns.title: Spatial Product Lab
patterns.quality: Interactive product inspection stage with green/gold spatial palette, live WebGL object, control chips, and product-lab posture instead of SaaS cards.

patterns.title: Kinetic Process Funnel
patterns.quality: Large scroll-led stages that make a workflow feel like a system turning on. Uses fewer cards and more movement, rhythm, and one-stage-at-a-time comprehension.

patterns.title: Luxury Editorial Command
patterns.description: $50K-grade bespoke editorial layout: full-bleed composition, architectural headline typography, strategic whitespace, staggered choreographed reveals, custom easing, and singular visual thesis. No card grids. No feature lists. One dominant idea per section.
patterns.quality: Architectural headline scale (clamp 3.5rem–9rem), letter-spacing -0.02em to -0.04em, line-height 0.9–1.05, weight contrast between display and body, ≥30% negative space in first viewport, staggered entrance with expo-out easing, at least one bespoke interaction treatment. Cannot be rebranded by logo swap.
fiftyKChecks: Display typeface at architectural scale — not system font
Intentional tracking and line-height on headline
Weight contrast between display and body
Staggered entrance: headline → subtext → CTA → visual
At least one bespoke hover/cursor/interaction treatment
Cannot be rebranded by logo swap
implementationNotes: Hero headline: font-size clamp(3.5rem, 8vw, 9rem); letter-spacing: -0.03em; line-height: 0.95;
Entrance variants: { hidden: { opacity: 0, y: 24 }, visible: (i) => ({ opacity: 1, y: 0, transition: { delay: i * 0.08, duration: 0.6, ease: [0.16, 1, 0.3, 1] } }) }

Scroll stagger: gsap.utils.toArray('.reveal').forEach((el, i) => { gsap.from(el, { scrollTrigger: { trigger: el, start: 'top 85%' }, opacity: 0, y: 32, duration: 0.7, delay: (i % 3) * 0.1, ease: 'expo.out' }); })
